title: Gochujang Buttered Udon
subtitle: Straight-to-wok · ready in 20 minutes
description: Garlicky, buttery udon in a glossy brick-red gochujang sauce that's sweet, savoury and tangy, with fried mushrooms and crispy lardons folded through at the end.

lardons.note: left out in the vegetarian version

steps.text: Heat a little {{oil}} in a large pan over medium-high. Fry the {{mushrooms}} and {{lardons}} until golden and crisp. Season, then remove and set aside.
In the same pan, melt the {{butter-garlic}} over medium-low. Add the {{garlic}}, season generously with {{salt-pepper}}, and cook, stirring, until softened but not browned.

Stir in the {{gochujang}}, {{honey}} and {{vinegar}}, and bring to a simmer over medium-high. Stir constantly until it reduces and turns glossy — a spatula dragged across the pan should leave a trail that holds for about 3 seconds. Remove from the heat.
Add the {{udon}} and the {{butter-finish}}, tossing to coat and heat through. Loosen with splashes of {{water}} until the sauce clings to the noodles.
Fold the fried {{mushrooms}} and {{lardons}} back in. Taste and season with {{salt-pepper}}, top with {{scallions}}, and serve immediately.

notes: Straight-to-wok udon needs no boiling — it goes straight into the sauce. Any udon works; cook per its packet first if using dried or frozen.
For the vegetarian version, just leave the lardons out and fry the mushrooms on their own.
Buy plain gochujang paste, not gochujang sauce (which adds vinegar and sugar). Oil the inside of the measuring cup so the paste slips out cleanly.
No starchy pasta water here, so keep a little plain hot water beside the pan to emulsify and loosen the sauce.

nutrition.note: Rough estimate for the version WITH lardons. Without them (vegetarian), figure roughly 595 kcal and 25g fat per serving. Approximate, not a lab analysis.
